title: How credits work
content:
## What you'll get

A quick overview of what credits are, which parts of building an app use them, and how to add more when you need to.

---

## What credits are

Credits are how Emergent measures usage. Every time the platform does work for you - writing code from a prompt, running tests, deploying your app - it uses a few credits from your account. You'll see your current balance in the top-right corner of the workspace.

This means you only pay for what you actually use, and costs stay predictable.

---

## What uses credits

Credits get deducted when the platform performs any of these tasks:

- **Code generation** - Each prompt that writes, changes or extends your app's code uses credits. Bigger changes and more complex files cost more.

- **Testing** - Automated tests (unit tests, integration checks, visual scans) all consume credits. More thorough test suites use more per run.

- **Deploying to production** - Building your app and pushing it live (including edge deployment and CDN updates) uses credits based on build time and app size.

- **Integrations & background tasks** - Calling third-party APIs, running scheduled jobs and background workers each deduct credits.

- **Database operations** - Heavy database work (large queries, bulk inserts) incurs small incremental charges.

- **LLM calls from your app** - If your *app itself* calls language models at runtime using [the Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key), those API calls are billed through your Emergent credits.

<Callout type="note" title="Maxx mode uses more">
When you turn on **Maxx mode** (the toggle in the prompt bar), the platform plans more carefully and runs deeper checks. You'll get higher-quality results, but it uses 2-4× the credits of a normal prompt.
</Callout>

---

## How much a prompt costs

A single prompt can use anywhere from a handful of credits (for a small UI fix) to hundreds (for a full feature with tests and deployment). The platform shows you an **estimated cost** before committing big changes.

<Callout type="tip" title="Set a spending limit">
In **Settings → Billing**, you can set a **maximum credits per prompt**. If a task would go over that limit, Emergent will ask you to approve it or break it into smaller steps - so you never get a surprise bill.
</Callout>

---

## Checking your balance & topping up

The workspace sidebar shows a real-time **credit meter** with your current balance and this month's trend. Click it to see a breakdown by category (generation, testing, deploy, integrations) and which prompts cost the most.

You'll get an email alert when your balance drops below 20 % of your monthly allowance.

**To add more credits:**
- **One-time top-ups** never expire and roll over indefinitely.
- **Monthly plan credits** roll over for up to three billing cycles, then expire.
- Emergent always spends expiring credits first, so you get the most value.

<Callout type="warning" title="If you hit zero">
If your balance reaches zero during a build or deploy, the operation will pause. You can resume immediately by adding credits - no work is lost, but your app won't go live until the deploy finishes.
</Callout>

---

## Want more detail?

For a complete breakdown of credit rates, volume discounts and billing mechanics, see the full [How credits work](/how-credits-work) reference.
description: What uses credits, what doesn't, and what a first app typically costs.
